content:
Maya Patel: Acme reported a p95 jump (~2x) after we onboarded acme-llama-v2-2026. Happens only on long-context requests (>12k tokens). Ticket: https://support.acme/example
Igor Petrov: can you paste an anonymized example of the payload they send?
Maya Patel: here's a trimmed sample they keep sending:
```json
{
  "model": "acme-llama-v2-2026",
  "input": "<very long doc...>",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "stream": false
}
```
Maya Patel: they say the regression aligns with when we flipped to tokenizer variant v2-bpe-pad-left during onboarding.
Sanjay Rao: timeline looks like: model onboarded -> tokenizer variant changed -> p95 spike for long requests. suspect pad_side change.
ops-bot: Deploy event: canary rollout for acme-llama-v2-2026 started by @ml-onboard-bot at 2026-01-15T12:03:40Z :rocket:
Igor Petrov: inspected their request traces. Token counts differ: old pad_right tokenization yields 12002 tokens, new pad_left yields 12006 and different leading tokens. That breaks KV cache reuse so runtime does full generation sometimes.
Maya Patel: they asked for root cause + repro. Can we produce a minimal repro and perf numbers?
Sanjay Rao: quick repro script I used against sandbox runtime:
```bash
# approximate repro
python3 perf_repro.py --model acme-llama-v2-2026 --pad-side left --context 18000 --repeat 100
# or curl to hosted API
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate | jq -r '.latency_ms'
```
Igor Petrov: perf on a local a100 sandbox:
- pad_right (legacy): p95 ~ 210ms
- pad_left (new): p95 ~ 515ms
p50/p90 similar; p95 spike points to occasional full recompute/cache misses.
Elin Chen: runtime logs show:
```
INFO runtime: kv_cache_miss=true reason=tokenizer_mismatch seq_hash=0xabc123
INFO runtime: falling_back_full_generation seq_len=12006
```
Maya Patel: customer provided traces around 2026-01-15T11:58Z showing intermittent full gens.
Sanjay Rao: hypothesis: pad_left shifts token positions relative to pad_right, so cache keys (which include token positions) don't match existing cached prefixes -> miss.
Igor Petrov: confirmed pad_token_id and pad_side are both exposed on tokenizer. We can normalize by stripping padding before cache-key generation to preserve alignment.
Elin Chen: proposed mitigations:
- short term: server-side normalizer that trims leading pad tokens and reindexes tokens before cache key creation (hotfix)
- immediate workaround: pin customer to pad-right variant of the model in catalog (we still keep that variant)
- medium term: change runtime to canonicalize tokens for cache keys regardless of pad_side (more invasive)
Maya Patel: Acme asked if we can roll them back to prior tokenizer variant now.
Igor Petrov: we can pin them to acme-llama-v2-2026-pad-right; I'll create a support rollback entry.
support-bot: Roll request created: support/1769810001-pin-acme-pad-right by @Maya Patel
Elin Chen: token diffs (start of arrays) explain the issue:
```
# pad-left tokens (start)
[0,0,17,504, ... 1024]
# pad-right tokens (start)
[17,504,...,1024,0,0]
```
The reorder changes seq_hash.
Sanjay Rao: short mitigation plan:
1) Pin customer to pad-right model variant.
2) Deploy pad-normalizer in runtime which strips leading pad tokens and recomputes canonical token arrays before cache-keying. Small change, feature-flagged.
3) Add e2e test: long docs tokenized with both pad sides must produce identical cache key.
Igor Petrov: opening PR runtime/kv-cache/normalize-pad. Will add metric kv_cache_miss_reason=pad_side and log kv_cache_normalizer=enabled.
ops-bot: Canary deploy started for runtime patch by @Igor Petrov at 2026-01-15T14:20:10Z
Sanjay Rao: monitoring: add a dashboard for kv_cache_miss_rate and segmentation by model/tokenizer. I'll own alerts.
Maya Patel: drafting customer update. Also asked about billing impact.
Elin Chen: p95 increase means extra compute for affected requests (~2x) when full-gen happens; for hosted customers that's latency only, cost impact is small for us. If Dedicated, bill surface might change. Recommend we state no immediate billing changes expected.
Maya Patel: draft to Acme: \"Root cause: tokenizer pad-side change during onboarding changed token ordering causing intermittent KV-cache misses for long-context requests. Temporary fix: pinned you to pad-right variant and we have a runtime canary to normalize padding. ETA 2-4h. No billing changes expected.\"
Igor Petrov: PR in progress. Adding unit tests to assert identical cache keys for pad-left/right permutations.
Sanjay Rao: will add monitoring alert to SRE queue.
Maya Patel: Acme replied: \"Thanks, seeing improved p95 on some requests already :thumbsup:\"
Elin Chen: follow-ups:
- eng-ml: include pad_side and tokenizer metadata in model manifest explicitly.
- devex/docs: update onboarding checklist to test pad_side with long-context corpora.
Igor Petrov: postmortem item: when tokenizer changes, always run synthetic long-context perf harness for both pad sides.
Maya Patel: closing action items: pin customer -> done, runtime PR -> canary, monitoring alert -> SRE assigned. I'll update ticket when full rollout complete. Thanks everyone <3
